previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient, a woman with end-stage liver disease from hepatitis C cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma, was admitted for abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea. Imaging revealed new moderate ascites and gallstones with mild gallbladder wall thickening, raising concern for cholecystitis. She remained afebrile without leukocytosis. Stool studies were negative for infectious causes, and blood cultures grew coagulase-negative staph in one bottle, likely a contaminant. Urine showed low-count Enterococcus. She was treated with ciprofloxacin and metronidazole for presumed mild cholecystitis, with symptom improvement. Her cirrhosis, diabetes, myasthenia gravis, and other comorbidities were managed without complication. She was discharged home on antibiotics and follow-up instructions, with stable condition and plans for outpatient liver clinic follow-up.

Brief Hospital Course:
# Post-procedure bleeding: Mrs. ___ was admitted from ___ suite 
after CT-guided biopsy and fiduciary seed placement.  She had 
come in for radio frequency ablation of her hepatic tumor 
(likely HCC), however, this was not done for fear of heat sink 
effect on IVC.  Due to concern of bleeding and thrombocytopenia, 
patient was given 1 bag of platelets and 2 units of FFP prior to 
the procdure.  There were no known complications from the 
procedure, however, in observation afterwards, she was noted to 
have a drop in hematocrit from 32 to 28.5.  Due to risk of 
bleeding, she was admitted to ___ 10.  Propanolol was held so 
possible tachycardia from hemorrhage would not be masked.  
Serial hct at 6 hour intervals were drawn and while stable 
overnight, her hematocrit was noted to be 25 on the morning 
after the procedure.  On exam vitals were stable, there was no 
sign of active bleeding through the biopsy site nor was there 
evidence of intra-abdominal hemorrhage--patient had no 
abdominal, signs of peritonitis or ecchymoses.  She was 
transfused 2 units of FFP and 1 unit of PRBCS.  She was 
monitored overnight and hematocrit was stable.  On discharge, 
she was hemodynamically stable.

radiology_notes.text:
CLINICAL INDICATION:  Cirrhosis and liver mass concerning for hepatocellular
carcinoma.

Ultrasound guidance was used for planning purposes for liver mass biopsy and
fiducial seed placement.  Please refer to the separately dictated CT report,
clip ___.

CLINICAL INDICATION:  Cirrhosis and suspected hepatocellular carcinoma. Please
perform radiofrequency ablation.

PHYSICIANS:  ___.

COMPLICATIONS:  None immediate.

MEDICATIONS:  General anesthesia, local lidocaine.

PROCEDURE NOTE:  Following a discussion of the risks, benefits and
alternatives of the procedure, informed written consent was obtained.  The
patient was brought to radiology, intubated and placed on the CT table in the
supine position.  Limited ultrasound of the right upper quadrant was
performed.  An appropriate skin site was chosen, and the skin was prepped and
draped in sterile fashion.  1% lidocaine was used for local anesthetic.
Attempt was made at placing a 17-gauge introducer needle into the hepatic dome
mass; however, this was technically difficult under US guidance, and the
decision was made to proceed with CT guidance.  Under CT/fluoroscopic
guidance, the 17- gauge introducer needle was advanced to the level of the
hepatic dome mass and two 18-gauge core biopsies were obtained. Cytology was
present and stated that the specimens were likely inadequate; however, given
the proximity of the hepatic veins, further biopsies were not obtained.  Also,
due to the proximity of this lesion to the hepatic veins and IVC and
suboptimal visualization, radiofrequency ablation could not be performed.
Following a discussion with the referring clinician, the decision was made to
place fiducial seeds for subsequent gamma-knife therapy. Two seeds were
therefore placed, and positioning was confirmed with CT.  The introducing
needle was removed and hemostasis was achieved with manual pressure.  The
patient tolerated the procedure well, with no immediate complications.  

Dr. ___ was present for the entire procedure.

FINDINGS:  Preprocedure CT demonstrates minimal dependent consolidation and
ground-glass, likely representing aspiration from intubation.  Again noted is
a nodular contour of the liver, consistent with cirrhosis.  There is a subtle
hypodense lesion near the confluence of the hepatic veins, corresponding with
previously seen hypervascular lesion.  Numerous gallstones are seen within an
otherwise unremarkable gallbladder.  Again noted is post Roux-en-Y appearance
of the stomach.

Post-procedural CT demonstrates minimal increase in free fluid around the
liver of intermediate density, likely representing a small amount of
hemorrhage.  Fiducial seeds are identified.

IMPRESSION:

Status post core biopsy of hepatic dome lesion and fiducial seed placement. RF
ablation was not performed due to very close proximity of the lesion to the
IVC (heat sink effect) and suboptimal visualization.
